mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals a shift to monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value weights on future cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers a risk-off reaction, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in rate-hike periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals a shift to monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value weights on future cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 1% for 3 consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strong-labor periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decrease in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding -1% for 3 consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer and business confidence, compressing discount rates, and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in weak-labor periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 1% for 3 consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in strong-labor periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for 3 consecutive months signals a strengthening supply-side capacity, which supports corporate earnings growth and reduces discount-rate pressure, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strong-supply periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding -2% for 3 consecutive months signals a supply-side contraction, which compresses discount rates and reduces growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in weak-supply periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
